4. Designation 

4.1 Taper plug gauges shall be designated by the diameter </ 2 of the handle bore to be checked 
and the number of this standard* 

Example: 

A taper plug gauge used to check the taper bore of handle whose diameter d 2 is 2*5 
shall be designated as: 

Taper Plug Gauge 2"5 IS : 9529 

4.2 Taper ring gauge shall be designated by the diameter d 2 of taper shank of the gauging members 
and the number of this standard. 



Example: 



A taper ring gauge used to shank the taper shank of the gauging member (plain and 
threaded ) whose diameter d* is 2'5 shall be designated as: 

Tanar Rinn Canno O'R IS • G59Q 

5. General Requirements — Other requirements not covered in this standard shall conform to 
IS: 7018 (Part l)-1973. 

6. Marking 

6.1 Taper Plug Gauge — Shall be marked with the taper to be checked, corresponding handle number 
to be checked and the manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 



13:9529-1180 

8.2 Taper Ring Gauge — Shall be marked with the taper to be checked, the corresponding handle 
number of the taper shank to be checked and the manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 

6.3 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

These gauges are for the manufacture and verification of taper lock shanks and taper bore 
handles. Ring gauges may also be used to control the accuracy of the tools used for producing the 
handles. 

The plug gauge when firmly applied to handle shall be a good fit without shake and end face 
of each end of the handle shall lie between the large end face of the plug gauge and the step face. 

In order to access the accuracy taper of producing operation, a light film of marking blue may 
be applied to the gauge and the contact area observed. If there is any variation in taper, it is prefer- 
able for contact to be hard at the large end diameter of the taper. 

The ring gauge applied to a taper shank shall assemble firmly and the small end of the taper 
shank shall lie between the end face of the ring gauge and step face. A light film of marking blue 
may be applied to the shank and the contact area observed. If there is any variation in taper, it is 
preferable for contact to be hard at the large end diameter of the taper. 

The ring gauge may be used for the control or verification of the accuracy of the tool used to 
produce taper. For this purpose, light film of marking blue should be applied to each cutting land 
'of the tool or to the surface of the gauge and the contact area observed. If there is any variation 
between the taper, it is preferable for the contact to be hard at the small end diameter of taper. 

This standard is based on ISO 3670-1979 ' Blanks for plug gauges and handles ( taper lock and 
trilock) and ring gauges — DesiQn and general dimensions', issued by the International Organiza- 
tion for Standardization.
